meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'art director', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: Vika works as the restaurant art director.
This is Viktoria Sergeyevna, our art director.
I am the art director of the restaurant.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry', paired with 'забеспокоиться'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
Mum is worried.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to fit in, blend into a team or setting
meanings.note: integrate smoothly into a social group or environment

examples.trans: You fit into the team perfectly.

examples.text: Новичок быстро вписался в рабочий ритм.
examples.trans: The newcomer quickly blended into the work rhythm.

examples.text: Похоже, ты отлично вписываешься в коллектив!
examples.trans: Looks like you fit right into the team!

meanings.note: Ordinal number. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.trans: This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have visitors!
We're going visiting.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.
The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Physical combat or brawl. Common feminine noun meaning 'fight, brawl, scuffle' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A noisy fight broke out on the street.
Stop this senseless fight!
Stop this fight right now!

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'стрелить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to shoot', forming an aspectual pair with 'застреливать'.

examples.text: Если шеф узнает про испорченный торт, он нас просто застрелит взглядом!
examples.trans: If the chef finds out about the ruined cake, he will simply shoot us down with a glare!

examples.text: Герой старого фильма грозился застрелить своего главного соперника.
examples.trans: The hero of the old movie threatened to shoot his main rival.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, please.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: concluding sum or recap of an event

examples.trans: Let's sum up the first week.

examples.text: В итоге все остались очень довольны.
examples.trans: In the end everyone remained very satisfied.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: all the people working together in an organisation

examples.trans: The staff forced me into this.

examples.text: У нас на работе очень дружный коллектив.
examples.trans: We have a very friendly team at work.

examples.text: Я своё мнение не менял. Это меня коллектив заставил.
examples.trans: I haven't changed my opinion. The staff forced me into this.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It's better like this.
I feel better today.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: намного хуже = much worse; намного лучше = much better

examples.trans: In prison it will be much worse.
Today is much warmer.

examples.text: Но я же вижу, как тебе плохо. В тюрьме будет намного хуже, поверь мне.
examples.trans: But I can see how bad things are for you. In prison it will be much worse, believe me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

examples.trans: I've been waiting a week.
The sea in a week!

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: trouble or disturbance caused to others

examples.trans: Sorry for the inconvenience caused.

examples.text: Шум в зале создал большие неудобства.
examples.trans: The noise in the dining room caused great inconvenience.

examples.text: Вот вам щедрые деньги за эти неудобства.
examples.trans: Here is generous money for these inconveniences.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.trans: I promise you.
You promised!

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya!
The suit fits you great.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.en: to poison, intoxicate with venom or toxic substance
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'равить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to poison', forming an aspectual pair with 'отравлять'.

examples.text: В первый день ты чуть не отравил гостя.
examples.trans: On the first day you almost poisoned a guest.
The spoiled dish could have poisoned people.

meanings.note: С первого раза = the first time. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.trans: This is my first day.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pistol, handgun' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Stop, why did you take a pistol?
The officer put the pistol away in its holster.

examples.text: Стой, ты зачем пистолет взял? Ты что, с ума сошёл? Дай сюда!
examples.trans: Stop, why did you take a pistol? Are you out of your mind? Give it here!

meanings.note: Disappoint expectations. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let down, fail', paired with 'подводить'.

examples.trans: I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: May I go?
Let's go home.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.trans: Maybe you could help?
Of course I'll help.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: очень похоже = that's just like him
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хоже').

examples.trans: That's just like him!
It looks like rain.

examples.text: Правда похоже. А может, вы сами позвоните губернатору?
examples.trans: It really is. Why don't you call the governor yourself?

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Рабочее место = job, workplace. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').
As a noun. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A working day.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.
She's glad.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: provoke intense anger or irritation

examples.trans: You angered the chief art director.

examples.text: Его резкие слова сильно разозлили шефа.
examples.trans: His sharp words infuriated the chef greatly.
You angered our chief art director.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
Summer is coming soon.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Give me the keys.
Come here!
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: You're fired!
He was fired.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Transitive verb. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'строить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrange, cause', paired with 'устраивать'.

A disturbance. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'строить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrange, cause', paired with 'устраивать'.

examples.trans: To cause disturbances.
To organize a holiday for children.

examples.text: Он устроил беспорядки прямо на городской улице.
examples.trans: He caused disturbances right on the city street.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Чуть-чуть = a tiny bit. Core Russian adv meaning 'a little; nearly' in everyday speech.
чуть не + verb: я чуть не упал = I nearly fell

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Common substantive noun meaning 'noise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Where is this noise coming from?

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

meanings.note: Giving freely. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('generous').

examples.trans: You are a very generous person.
Thank you for the generous gift.

examples.text: Извините, вы очень щедрый, а я неловкий. Я пойду попробую приготовить себе кашу.
examples.trans: Forgive me, you are very generous, and I am clumsy. I will go try to cook myself some porridge.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
